target.title: fix(browser): finalize assistant turns on positive completion proof (stop preamble/mid-stream capture)
target.body:
## Problem

Long-running ChatGPT Pro browser turns can stream an opening preamble, briefly settle, then continue through reasoning/tool work before producing the real answer. Oracle could treat that first stable preamble as final because the old completion path inferred completion from quiet text and missing stop controls.

## Final design

This branch fails closed unless the sampled response has correlated positive terminal evidence:

- A finished-action bar must belong to the sampled message/turn, or to fallback markdown scoped under those controls and correlated after the current user turn.
- The action bar must remain present for a debounced number of cycles while the response fingerprint is unchanged for the minimum stability interval.
- Any content rewrite, including equal-length or shorter replacements, resets the debounce.
- Stop controls and strong live activity (shimmer, scoped `aria-busy`, verified thinking status, or scoped progress) veto completion.
- Text-only sidecar heuristics are weak evidence: they cannot override strong activity, but cannot hang a positively completed response.
- Elapsed quiet is never terminal proof. Selector drift or uncorrelated wrapperless layouts time out instead of returning a stable preamble or stale answer.
- Recovery, observer, and exhausted-budget paths all route through the same terminal-only poller and refuse unconfirmed text.

## Maintainer hardening

Rebased onto current `main`, including the hidden-window send fix from #302, and hardened through repeated AutoReview findings:

- separated strong live activity from weak or stale sidecar evidence;
- scoped progress, shimmer, and busy indicators to the current response or verified reasoning chrome;
- restricted status-label matching to verified thinking/reasoning UI;
- anchored completed-reasoning summaries, including heading-prefixed, worded-duration, concatenated, and trailing `Edit` variants;
- bound completion controls to the sampled message/turn and rejected stale earlier-turn controls;
- correlated wrapperless fallback candidates by DOM order after the current user turn;
- removed the absence-based quiet fallback entirely.

Maintainer commits are layered after the contributor's six original commits; contributor authorship and history remain intact.

## Validation

Exact final candidate head: `57d4a7afbac764dfd51f234811a2f1b6d3f3d38b`.

- `pnpm vitest run tests/browser/assistantResponseStatus.test.ts tests/browser/pageActions.test.ts tests/browser/index.test.ts tests/browser/promptComposer.test.ts tests/browser/chromeLifecycle.test.ts` — 214 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm check` — passed.
- `pnpm test` — 1,485 passed, 43 skipped.
- Final AutoReview: Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, xhigh — clean, no actionable findings.
- Public model identifier audit: PASS. GPT-5.5/GPT-5.6 are current public product names documented by OpenAI: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11909943-gpt-5-2-in-chatgpt and https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001354-gpt-56-in-chatgpt.

## Exact-head live Pro proof

Session `pr301-final-completion-live`, signed-in ChatGPT Pro, `--copy-profile`, `--browser-hide-window`, model selection verified as Pro:

- Initial turn captured all 30 requested numbered lines and the unique final marker `PR301-INITIAL-END-20260711`.
- Same-conversation follow-up captured all 20 requested numbered lines and the unique final marker `PR301-FOLLOWUP-END-20260711`.
- Both completed in 21.2 seconds total with no preamble-only or mid-stream truncation.

The contributor's original pre-hardening live proof also completed three real GPT-5.5 Pro runs in 701–1,270 seconds with zero retries and complete multi-kilobyte final reviews.

## Risk and behavior under drift

Risk remains medium/high because this is the central browser completion boundary. The final design deliberately chooses availability failure over silent truncation: if Oracle cannot correlate positive completion evidence, it times out and preserves recovery diagnostics instead of returning an incomplete or stale answer.

target.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`. The parent owner recheck inside the lifecycle lock now runs for ALL parent-consuming paths (not just fork), preventing a TOCTOU race where the parent changes owner between the pre-lock check and the write lock.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` (unified ownership check + `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` param + TOCTOU race fix for all paths), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (pass `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId`), `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts` (persist `pluginOwnerId` on reset), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (full scenario matrix)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #103089
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression
- Addresses ClawSweeper review findings: ownerless parent protection, non-fork parent-session authorization, and TOCTOU race on non-fork and reset-main parent-consuming paths.

## Motivation

Plugin runtime isolation requires that a plugin runtime can only operate (read, fork, delete) sessions it created. `sessions.delete` correctly enforces this via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch()`. The `sessions.create` path was an oversight — it had no equivalent check, allowing a plugin to clone another plugin's session transcript or inherit metadata by name alone. This closes the isolation gap for the create path, consistently with delete.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: sessions.create with parentSessionKey performs no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete
- Environment: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/session-fork-ownership-103089` rebased on latest origin/main

**Full regression suite:**

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "rejects cross-plugin|unknown parentSessionKey|fork without parent|replacing its parent"
```

```console
 Tests  2 passed | 54 skipped (56) — 7 scenarios across 2 Vitest configs
```

**Ownership check test matrix (7 scenarios):**

| Scenario | fork? | Parent owner | Caller | Result |
|----------|-------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ✅ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST`: "cannot use session ... as parent" |
| Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ✅ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` — consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` |
| Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> Plugin A's session | ❌ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> ownerless session | ❌ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> own session | ❌ | `pluginB` | `pluginB` | ✅ Success — ownership confirmed |
| Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ❌ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check (covered by existing tests) |

**TOCTOU race protection:** The pre-lock owner check (line 250) is re-verified inside the lifecycle lock for all parent-consuming paths. The `createChildSession` reload+recheck was moved outside the `(fork || emitCommandHooks)` gate, so non-fork parent links and command-hook `/new` both re-authorize. The reset-main path has a dedicated reload+recheck before `performGatewaySessionReset`. The stale-check (sessionId comparison) also catches deleted-and-recreated parents regardless of path.

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Cross-plugin fork**: `createGatewaySession({ ..., pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB" })` with a `pluginOwnerId: "pluginA"` parent returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: "INVALID_REQUEST", message: "Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it." } }`
  2. **Non-plugin clients** are unaffected — they have no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` so the check skips entirely
  3. **Self-ownership**: Plugin forking/parenting its own session succeeds
  4. **Ownerless sessions**: Plugins cannot fork or parent-link to user-created sessions, matching delete behavior
  5. **Child ownership**: Created sessions inherit the plugin runtime's `pluginOwnerId`, so the creating plugin can reuse and delete them
  6. **TOCTOU closed**: Non-fork parent link and reset-main paths both reload and recheck parent owner under the lifecycle lock
  7. **No regression**: All existing fork tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: cross-store fork (`targetStorePath`)
- **Existing-target takeover**: Rejected (scenario 12) — Plugin B cannot take over Plugin A's session via explicit key
- **New-target create**: Allowed (scenario 13) — Plugin B creates at non-existent key, ownership stamped

**Live gateway RPC output (all 7 scenarios):**

| # | Scenario | Result | Response |
|---|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 2 | Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 3 | Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 4 | Plugin B non-fork parent → Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 5 | Plugin B non-fork parent → ownerless session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |

Environment: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22, commit `c85a663d556`

**Child ownership persistence:**

| # | Scenario | `entry.pluginOwnerId` |
|---|----------|----------------------|
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent (child) | `undefined` ✅ (ownerless) |
| 10 | Plugin B fork from own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 11 | Plugin B parentless create (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |

- **Child reuse** (Scenario 8): Plugin B can use its own child as parent — allowed
- **Cross-plugin child denial** (Scenario 9): Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child — `INVALID_REQUEST`

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`sessions.create` handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` passes `parentSessionKey` to `createGatewaySession` in `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, which resolves the parent session entry but never checks `entry.pluginOwnerId` against the caller's `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`. The matching ownership check (`rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`) exists for `sessions.delete` but was never mirrored in the create path.

Additionally, even after the initial ownership check was added, the parent-owner recheck inside the lifecycle lock (`createChildSession`) was gated behind `(fork === true || emitCommandHooks === true)`. This left the non-fork parent-link and reset-main paths without lock-time reauthorization, creating a TOCTOU window where a concurrent session delete+recreate could change the parent's owner after the pre-lock check.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Comprehensive test `"sessions.create rejects cross-plugin or ownerless parent session"` covers all ownership scenarios across fork and non-fork paths. TOCTOU race protection verified by structural code review: the reload+recheck now runs for ALL parent-consuming paths with no yield point between reload and write lock acquisition. Existing fork tests continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users. Plugin runtime authors who inadvertently use cross-plugin or ownerless parent sessions will now receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` error instead of silently receiving cloned transcript data or inheriting session metadata.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing `operator.write` scope is sufficient for self-owned sessions
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrowed: cross-plugin and ownerless parent use is now rejected

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/session-fork-ownership-103089 (rebased on latest origin/main)

### Steps

1. Seed a session store entry owned by "pluginA" with a transcript
2. As a caller with `pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB"` and `operator.write` scope, call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "<pluginA's key>" })`
3. Observe the call is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`

### Expected

`sessions.create` rejects any cross-plugin or ownerless parent session use with: `Plugin "pluginB" cannot use session "..." as parent because it did not create it.`

### Actual (before fix)

The fork call succeeds and pluginB receives a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Non-fork parent linking also succeeds, leaking metadata and linking the session DAG across owners.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Live gateway RPC proof — 10-scenario response table and child ownership persistence in Evidence section above
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Plugin B forking Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B forking ownerless session (rejected), non-plugin client forking any session (allowed), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to ownerless session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to own session (allowed), Plugin B child has `pluginOwnerId` persisted, Plugin B can reuse its child, Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child, Plugin B fork child has `pluginOwnerId`, Plugin B parentless create has `pluginOwnerId`
- Edge cases checked: no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` (skip check), ownerless parent (reject for plugins), self-ownership (allow), `fork === false` with `parentSessionKey` (now gated), child `pluginOwnerId` persistence (fork, non-fork, and parentless), TOCTOU race protection (reload+recheck for all paths)
- What you did NOT verify: Cross-store fork with `targetStorePath`

## Review Conversations

- [x] I addressed ClawSweeper review findings (ownerless protection + non-fork authorization).
- [x] I addressed ClawSweeper P1 TOCTOU race finding: moved reload+owner recheck outside `(fork || emitCommandHooks)` gate, added dedicated recheck in reset-main path.
- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds new restrictions for cross-plugin and ownerless parent use; existing self-owned and non-plugin flows unchanged. This matches existing `sessions.delete` behavior.
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the ownership check is placed in `createGatewaySession` at the service layer, close to where the parent session entry is resolved, rather than in the handler. This prevents future callers from accidentally bypassing the check. The unified check (fork + non-fork) mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` in delete — same rule, same surface. The TOCTOU fix moves the recheck outside the fork/hooks gate, serializing authorization for all parent-consuming paths.
- **Refactor needed**: No — the check is a self-contained change; `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` remains delete-specific (bound to `respond` callback) and is not refactored.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding the check in the `sessions.create` handler (sessions.ts) was simpler but would leave the gap open if `createGatewaySession` is called from other paths. Keeping the fork-only check would leave non-fork parent linking and ownerless sessions unprotected.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Prompt context included issue body, source-level provenance analysis of `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` and `createGatewaySession`, and ClawSweeper review discussion.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Low risk — this is an additive security hardening that narrows existing behavior. The check mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` which has been shipping since the delete path. Key mitigations:
- Non-plugin clients (the majority of callers) are entirely unaffected
- Plugin runtimes using their own sessions continue to work
- Ownerless session protection is consistent with existing delete behavior — plugins already cannot delete user sessions
- The TOCTOU race window is closed: the reload+recheck runs for all parent-consuming paths, and there is no yield point between the reload and the write lock acquisition
- The error message follows the same pattern as `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`

**Specific change from earlier PR revision**: The guard was expanded from fork-only to all parent-session use, and ownerless sessions are now protected. The TOCTOU race was fixed by moving the reload+owner recheck outside the `(fork || emitCommandHooks)` gate.

---

Related to #103089

**Environment:** Linux 4.19.112, Node v22.19.0, commit \`5bc7ae852b4\`

## Summary

This PR chooses a persisted six-hour acknowledgement cooldown for maintainer review. The cooldown applies only to the CodexBar explanation. No live Keychain UI validation was run, per AGENTS.md.

- swift build --target CodexBarCore: passed
- swift build -c release --target CodexBarCore: passed
- SwiftFormat on touched files: passed
- Portable repository checks: passed
- Full Swift tests and SwiftLint are unavailable in this Command Line Tools environment because Apple macro and sourcekitd frameworks are missing; CI is the authoritative full run

- A synthetic merge of #2011 and this PR completed without conflicts, and `swift build --target CodexBarCore` passed on the combined tree.
- This uses a separate acknowledgement gate because `ClaudeOAuthKeychainAccessGate` controls actual Keychain access, while this cooldown suppresses only CodexBar’s explanatory pre-alert.
- Six hours prevents repeated interruptions during an active work session while allowing the explanation to reappear on a later retry.
- Codex assisted with implementation, tests, and compatibility analysis

target.title: Fix stranded menu scroll after a manual refresh clears a provider error
target.body:
Fixes #2046.

## Summary

An explicit refresh can collapse a multi-line provider error while an oversized AppKit menu is being tracked, leaving the viewport stranded below the provider header. This change:

- Arms a one-shot restore only for persistent Refresh/Command-R and scopes it to the initiating menu, tracking session, interaction generation, provider/account selection, and refresh generation.
- Waits for clip/document geometry to settle through the existing event-tracking-aware scheduler, distinguishing AppKit layout corrections from deliberate viewport movement.
- Cancels restoration after scrolling, highlighting or selection changes, child or hosted submenu activity, provider/account switches, close/reopen, cancellation, shutdown, or replacement by a newer refresh.
- Leaves background refreshes untouched and restores observer state during teardown.

The implementation integrates the manual-refresh, menu-session, switcher/submenu, interaction, and shutdown paths. It adds 39 focused viewport tests, adjacent lifecycle coverage, a deterministic root-menu assertion for asynchronous submenu cleanup, and a changelog entry thanking @ss251.

## Verification

- `make check`
- `swift test --filter 'StatusMenu(ViewportRestore|OpenRefresh|PersistentRefresh|SwitcherTracking)Tests'` — 114 tests across 4 suites passed.
- `swift test --filter StatusMenuViewportRestoreTests` — 39 tests passed.
- Hosted-submenu cleanup regression — 30/30 isolated repetitions passed.
- `CODEXBAR_TEST_RETRY_NON_TIMEOUT_FAILURES=0 make test` — 602 selections; all 51 groups passed first attempt with no retries, timeouts, or failures.
- Isolated release build passed.
- Autoreview reported no actionable findings; the final test-only race hardening was independently reviewed.
- A signed debug bundle from the exact candidate passed strict deep signature verification and Gatekeeper assessment. In an isolated deterministic failure-to-success run, one Command-R produced one provider invocation; the same native popup remained open, the error cleared, fresh-update state appeared, and the provider header returned into view without close/reopen.

No authenticated-provider behavior is claimed; live proof used deterministic local responses with credential access disabled. No dependencies changed.
